Diego / Liam — attaching the up-to-date matrix. Summary below:

- What changed in last 90 days: BrightLayer (analytics) replaced LogixInsights as our telemetry aggregator for aggregated usage metrics. BrightLayer will process de-identified usage metrics and service-level telemetry; they do not receive raw production prompts or completions.
- Locations: BrightLayer operates primarily in US (us-west-2) but also has a data pipeline for aggregated logs in eu-west-1 for EU customers; for Finovate's account (US region) the data path is US-only.
- Retention: telemetry retention increased from 90 -> 180 days for aggregated metrics; audit logs retention unchanged.
- Access: BrightLayer has SOC2 Type II (docs attached in matrix), limited to engineering/devops personas; no external support staff have access to raw customer content.
- CDN: Nimbus CDN remains our edge provider; edge cache nodes may be located in multiple regions to optimize latency but content cached is only non-sensitive assets and truncated preview metadata.

Two caveats to flag:
1) Splunk (log archival) is used for system-level logs. For US accounts Splunk archival is in us-east-1; for a small subset of diagnostic exports (IP addresses in error traces) we may route to splunk-cloud eu-west-1 for aggregated monitoring in cross-region outfits — however we do not export actual customer message content there.
2) If Finovate requests a strictly US-only subprocessor footprint (no EU routing at all), we can offer an amendment to the DPA and update routing/pinning config — this will require a 30-day notice and coordination with our ops team.

I've attached the matrix and a simplified data-export diagram. Let me know if you need signed attestations or the SOC reports.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts — Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heads up: Finovate vendor re-org and subprocessor list request

Quick technical note to clarify Lauren's summary:

- Production prompt/completion content: Always stored in customer-controlled project namespaces and persisted to encrypted object storage in us-east-1 for Finovate's account. We do not forward raw prompt/completion content to third-party analytics vendors.
- Aggregated telemetry: BrightLayer receives aggregated usage metrics (no raw content). That stream contains service-level metrics, anonymized latencies, and counts. IPs are hashed when included in telemetry and are not reversible.
- Logs & diagnostics: System metrics and error traces are archived to Splunk for long-term retention. For accounts with strict regional requirements we can pin Splunk ingestion to us-east-1 only; doing so requires a configuration change and a 30-day lead time.
- CDN caching: edge previews are artifact-only (no full user content). Cache invalidation workflows are documented in the matrix.

If you want, we can generate a short attestation statement for Finovate that confirms: (1) no raw customer message content is shared with third-party analytics, (2) telemetry is pseudonymized, and (3) we can support a US-only pipeline with 30 days' notice.

— Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
